What happened: AMD-Anthropic deal: up to 2 GW of MI450 Helios racks from 1H 2027; AMD commits up to $5B equity investment in Anthropic.
Why it matters: Textbook vendor financing: AMD funds a customer that buys its chips; investment is paid out as deliveries happen.

What happened: AMD closes record $4.75B bond sale at A1/A ratings.
Why it matters: AMD shifts from net-cash simplicity toward borrowing to fund inventory, capacity and customer support ahead of the AI ramp.

What happened: Q3: record $13.4B revenue (+45%), Data Center $8.5B (+97%), Q4 guide ~$17B; but FCF only $554M as inventory jumped $3B; $1.2B warrant remeasurement charge.
Why it matters: Profits rising but cash is being tied up in inventory/receivables; the 10-Q revealed $8.5B of partner guarantees, $13.3B of leases to sublease and $6.2B of capacity backstops.

What happened: Goldman: chipmaker CDS (incl. AMD ~147bp) rise above hyperscalers for first time.
Why it matters: Credit markets are starting to price chip suppliers as lenders to the AI buildout.

What happened: TensorWave signs 6-yr, 457 MW AMD MI455X/Helios compute deal for OpenAI, online 1H 2027-early 2028.
Why it matters: OpenAI volume flowing through a neocloud intermediary - the kind of partner AMD's lease guarantees and capacity backstops support.

What happened: Anthropic IPO at $83; AMD buys $2.5B in concurrent private placement; Anthropic fell 8.5% on day two and AMD fell sharply.
Why it matters: AMD now holds marked-to-market equity in a customer; customer stock weakness hits AMD twice (investment value and demand confidence).

What happened: Hunterbrook short report on China/IEIT firmware plus new US license rule for 5 Asian/LatAm countries; AMD -8% Nov 19 and ~-13% Nov 20.
Why it matters: Regulatory risk to the Asia shipment pipeline that backs the Q4 and 2027 ramp; AMD denies the claims.

What happened: Q3 2026: sales $201.9B, AWS +39% to $46.0B, backlog $578B; capex $77.3B (~$20B above expectations); TTM FCF -$42.4B; EPS $1.89 missed; stock fell >7% after hours; 2027 capex to be 'meaningfully more'.
Why it matters: Amazon is now spending more than it earns in cash and plans to spend even more next year -- the gap is being filled with debt.

What happened: 10-Q: long-term debt $173.1B vs $65.6B at year-start; total commitments $883.6B incl. $164.9B unstarted leases; completed $50B OpenAI investment with final $21.3B in Q3.
Why it matters: Shows both the on-balance debt surge and the larger off-balance commitments a ratio-based scorer would miss.

What happened: Anthropic S-1 shows $110B committed to AWS through 2036 and $114.5B to Google; Anthropic is also renting its own datacenters ('Anthropic Direct' via Fluidstack).
Why it matters: Amazon's biggest AI customer is both funded by Amazon and starting to compete with AWS, limiting future AWS growth from it.

What happened: Anthropic priced a record $81.3B IPO at $83/share, ~ $1.5T valuation.
Why it matters: Validates Amazon's ~$238.7B paper stake (and gives a liquid asset it could monetize), but also means Amazon's equity cushion is partly tied to AI-lab valuations.

What happened: Amazon sold its first sterling bonds, pushing 2026 borrowing past $92B across USD, EUR, CHF, CAD, GBP.
Why it matters: Tapping every currency market signals how much external financing the capex plan needs.

What happened: $25B 'surprise' bond required 18-21bp extra yield; demand fell to 2.5x cover.
Why it matters: Early sign investors are demanding more to fund AI debt -- the credit-tightening channel in the thesis.

What happened: Big Tech raised $253.4B of new long-term debt in nine months (~45% of capex); local opposition grows (Sunbury, Ohio voters barred >25MW datacenters, hitting a $2B AWS campus).
Why it matters: Debt-funded capex plus power/permit pushback raises the risk of stranded or delayed capacity.

What happened: FQ3: revenue $29.6B (+86%), AI semis $16.7B (+221%), FCF $13.7B; FY26 AI guide raised to $58B; targets ~$115B FY27 / ~$230B FY28; stock fell ~11% next day on margin pressure.
Why it matters: Huge cash generation is the cushion behind the guarantees, but growth now depends on a handful of AI labs.

What happened: Banks begin syndicating $42B of Broadcom-backstopped senior loans for Anthropic's chip order (two $21B tranches due 2033).
Why it matters: First big test of market appetite for vendor-guaranteed AI chip debt.

What happened: WSJ/Bloomberg: Broadcom seeking $30-50B+ financing from Apollo/Blackstone for OpenAI's 10 GW custom chip program.
Why it matters: Signals the backstop model will extend to OpenAI, another cash-burning lab.

What happened: $63B 'North Star' SPV for Anthropic closes; Broadcom 8-K discloses up to ~$43B residual value support.
Why it matters: Adds to the $29B June backstop: ~$72B of contingent exposure tied to one customer.

What happened: S&P revises Broadcom outlook to stable from positive over rising AI risk and off-balance-sheet financings; AVGO CDS hits record ~175bp.
Why it matters: Rating agencies and credit markets are now explicitly pricing Broadcom's hidden leverage.

What happened: Blackstone tells investors Anthropic should expect 'high double-B' ratings post-IPO; North Star junior debt priced >10%.
Why it matters: The counterparty behind Broadcom's backstops is sub-investment grade on its own.

What happened: Anthropic IPOs at $83; Broadcom buys $1B in concurrent $26B private placement.
Why it matters: Broadcom is now supplier, guarantor, potential lender and shareholder to the same customer.

What happened: CoreWeave shares fall 15.5% in a day; unsecured bond yields hit ~15-16%, CDS >1,000bp amid rumors about debt and financing access (later cited in 10-Q risk factors).
Why it matters: Unsecured funding window effectively closed; company now depends on asset-backed loans, converts, prepayments and equity.

What happened: Microsoft capex $45.2B misses, citing delayed third-party capacity deliveries; trims CY2026 capex to ~$170B; neoclouds sell off.
Why it matters: Microsoft was 67% of CoreWeave's 2025 revenue; delivery delays defer revenue while interest keeps accruing.

What happened: Democratic midterm sweep and 41 local data-center ballot measures; CoreWeave -9%, CDS ~1,140bp.
Why it matters: Political/permitting backlash slows new capacity, hitting the most leveraged builders first.

What happened: Microsoft shrinking its roster of neocloud partners and prioritizing own data centers (CNBC/Bloomberg); also winds down Oracle rental deal.
Why it matters: Key anchor customer reducing third-party reliance raises renewal and concentration risk for CoreWeave's backlog.

What happened: Q3 beat: revenue $3.66B (+168%), backlog $132.5B, FY guide raised; but net loss $709M, interest $846M, capex $14.5B, debt $47.5B; ~$9B prepayments expected.
Why it matters: Strong demand but growth is almost entirely debt- and prepayment-funded; interest cost exceeds operating profit.

What happened: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns; interim CEO Kress says Nvidia will be more selective on future investments and guarantees, existing neocloud commitments unchanged.
Why it matters: Nvidia is CoreWeave's supplier, ~10% shareholder and $6.3B capacity backstop; perceived support is central to lender confidence.

What happened: CoreWeave marketing >= $4B Meta-contract-backed IG loan at ~7.5% vs ~16% on its unsecured bonds.
Why it matters: Lenders underwrite CoreWeave's customers, not CoreWeave; access depends on keeping AA-rated customer contracts.

What happened: CoreWeave CDS widens to ~1,233bp as AI selloff spreads to credit.
Why it matters: Market prices a majority chance of default within five years.

What happened: Q3 2026: revenue $127.6B (+25%), first top-and-bottom-line miss in ~4 yrs; Cloud +103% to $30.7B; capex $51.4B, FCF -$9.1B; stock fell ~10%.
Why it matters: First negative FCF quarter shows the buildout now outruns internal cash generation, so debt and equity issuance fill the gap.

What happened: CFO keeps 2026 capex at $195-205B and says 2027 capex will 'increase significantly'; Google began renting third-party compute late Q3 with margin headwinds.
Why it matters: Spending is set to climb further, and renting third-party capacity adds more off-balance purchase commitments.

What happened: Anthropic IPO filing discloses $121.3B of compute commitments to Google through 2033; Google and Nvidia each to buy $10B of Anthropic stock in private placement.
Why it matters: Google's single biggest backlog customer is one it funds; customer pays Google partly with Google's own investment dollars.

What happened: Anthropic prices IPO at $83/share (~$1.5T valuation); Google to own ~13.4-14% (cap 14.99%).
Why it matters: Stake worth ~$140B+ inflates Alphabet's earnings via mark-to-market and makes Alphabet's results sensitive to Anthropic's stock price.

What happened: Alphabet prices C$6B bonds incl. 40-yr 6% note at noticeably wider spreads than its May deal.
Why it matters: Even an AA+ borrower is paying more as AI-capex supply floods credit markets — an early credit-tightening signal.

What happened: 10-Q reveals $48.0B data-center credit-derivative backstops, $16.2B energy guarantees, $6.6B TPU repurchase guarantees and $130.5B of uncommenced leases.
Why it matters: These contingent obligations are not debt on the balance sheet, so a ratio-based scorecard misses them.

What happened: Crux AI JV with Blackstone announced: Google backstops up to $10B and books $16.8B of related-party backlog from it.
Why it matters: Classic circular structure: the supplier guarantees the customer's financing and counts the customer's purchases as backlog.

What happened: Q3 2026: revenue $64.6B (+26%) but operating margin halved to 20% on $9.9B legal charge and AI costs; capex $34.9B, FCF -$2.1B; 2026 capex guide $135-145B, 2027 AI spend 'notably larger'.
Why it matters: Meta's internal cash no longer covers its buildout; it now relies on bond markets and off-balance JVs.

What happened: Meta creates new non-voting Class C stock via 1:1 stock dividend (effective Jan 2027) to 'finance its growth' and support capital raising.
Why it matters: Signals equity issuance to fund AI without diluting Zuckerberg's control.

What happened: New Mexico judge orders Meta to pay $25B penalty (15% interest during appeal) in Cambridge Analytica privacy case.
Why it matters: A large new cash claim on top of the $9.9B multistate AG settlement, competing with capex for cash.

What happened: 10-Q: max exposure to unconsolidated data-center JVs rises 49% to $68.4B ($41.5B RVGs); uncommenced leases $355.7B; non-cancelable commitments $454.5B.
Why it matters: The off-balance obligation stack is ~10x Meta's on-balance debt.

What happened: Meta sells $15B of USD bonds (30-yr at ~7.5%) and debut ~EUR9B euro deal; S&P outlook negative.
Why it matters: Borrowing costs are rising and a ratings agency is openly flagging downgrade risk tied to AI capex.

What happened: Meta enters new Texas data center JV (20% stake, ~$14B development cost), following Hyperion/Blue Owl template.
Why it matters: Meta keeps replicating the off-balance JV + RVG structure, so hidden exposure keeps compounding.

What happened: Meta expands CoreWeave deal by $21B through 2032 (total ~$35B); Nebius deal up to $27B (Mar 2026).
Why it matters: Meta is the anchor tenant whose contracts collateralize leveraged neoclouds' debt — if Meta cuts back, those lenders are exposed.

What happened: Fiscal Q1 FY27: revenue $92.3B, Azure +48%, commercial RPO $677B (+73%), capex $45.2B incl. finance leases; calendar-2026 capex trimmed to ~$170B; third-party GPU contracts delayed to H2.
Why it matters: Demand is strong but spending is now far above free cash flow growth, and delays at neocloud suppliers show the build-out is supply-chain fragile.

What happened: 10-Q shows datacenter leases signed but not commenced jumped to $364.6B from $329.1B one quarter earlier.
Why it matters: This is the largest hidden obligation -- ~10x reported debt -- and it is invisible to debt/EBITDA scoring until each lease starts.

What happened: Microsoft sold $25B of bonds in 10 tranches, its first US bond since 2017, with ~$115B of orders.
Why it matters: Even an AAA cash machine is now borrowing to fund AI capex; demand was strong, so credit markets are still open for top names.

What happened: Microsoft earned $10.0B from OpenAI arrangements in the quarter (~11% of revenue); OpenAI owes it $7.2B.
Why it matters: A large, growing slice of revenue and receivables depends on one customer that is itself loss-making and financed by its suppliers.

What happened: Bloomberg: Microsoft stepping back from ~$70.9B of neocloud deals (Nscale, Nebius, IREN) facing delays; walked from a ~$3B UK site; IREN -18%, Nebius -16%, CoreWeave -12%.
Why it matters: Shows Microsoft can push risk back onto leveraged suppliers -- good for Microsoft, bad for the neoclouds whose debt relies on Microsoft contracts.

What happened: Big Tech (Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft, Oracle) raised $253.4B of new long-term debt in nine months, ~45% of capex vs ~17% a year earlier.
Why it matters: Confirms the thesis that the build-out is increasingly debt-financed, even at the strongest balance sheets.

What happened: Moody's warns hyperscaler AI spending threatens credit quality; counts unstarted leases as debt-like.
Why it matters: Rating agencies already adjust for the leases a balance-sheet-only app misses.

What happened: Nvidia invests $2B in Nebius; Meta signs up-to-$27B five-year capacity deal around the same time.
Why it matters: Supplier funding plus a mega-contract that requires massive new GPU spending.

What happened: Nebius closes $5.75B convertible note offering, total debt reaches ~$14B by Sept 30 (from $4.1B at year-end 2025).
Why it matters: Debt more than tripled in nine months to fund the build.

What happened: After abandoning a high-yield bond, Nebius takes a $3.5B one-year secured bridge from Citi.
Why it matters: Short-dated, rising-margin debt signals bond markets are closing for neoclouds.

What happened: Q3: revenue $981M, but 2026 guide cut on third-party capacity delays (Microsoft NJ tranches slip to Q2 2027); 2026 capex raised to ~$27B, 2027 capex $40-45B; stock fell ~17%.
Why it matters: Spending rises while revenue timing slips; Microsoft has termination rights if delivery dates are missed.

What happened: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns; neocloud stocks sell off ('Neoclouds buckle under Nvidia scare').
Why it matters: Nebius's key supplier and 9.3% shareholder is in turmoil and later says it will be more selective backing neoclouds.

What happened: Reuters: Nvidia turmoil marks end of easy money; Nebius converts at 70 cents (>12% yield); stock down 57% since Oct 6.
Why it matters: Cost of new capital has jumped right when Nebius needs tens of billions.

What happened: Nvidia's Kress: will stay 'disciplined and selective' supporting neoclouds and is 'rigorously evaluating future investments, commitments, and guarantees'.
Why it matters: Vendor-financing backstop for neoclouds may shrink.

What happened: Nvidia agrees to guarantee up to $105B of credit support for SB Energy's Ohio PORTS-Pike campus leased 20 years to OpenAI.
Why it matters: Largest single off-balance exposure; Nvidia pays only if OpenAI (a heavily vendor-financed customer) defaults on rent.

What happened: Reuters: banks and investors grow wary of AI debt after selloff; neocloud bonds sold off, Nebius shelved a high-yield bond.
Why it matters: Nvidia's neocloud commitments only activate if neoclouds get financing; tighter credit hits Nvidia's fastest-growing customer segment.

What happened: Jensen Huang resigns as CEO after affair scandal tied to an alleged Chinese spy; CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO; Harvey Jones named first board chair; FBI investigating; stock fell ~14%.
Why it matters: Huang personally architected the customer-investment web; governance uncertainty triggered Moody's outlook cut and raises questions about future vendor financing policy.

What happened: Q3 FY27: revenue $115.8B (+103% y/y), Q4 guide $130B; supply commitments jump to $390B; guarantees $118B; Kress says Nvidia will be 'disciplined and selective' supporting neoclouds and is 'rigorously evaluating future investments, commitments, and guarantees'.
Why it matters: Strong cash flow but off-balance commitments grew faster than revenue; signal that vendor support for neoclouds may tighten.

What happened: Nvidia stops shipping licensed H200/Hopper chips to China after $2.4B in Q3; Q4 guidance assumes no China data center compute; Commerce issues rule curbing China's remote access to advanced chips (Nov 16); House committee releases H200 license records (Nov 19).
Why it matters: Removes a revenue stream and adds political/regulatory scrutiny at the same time as the CEO's China-linked scandal.

What happened: Moody's cuts Nvidia outlook to stable (Aa1 affirmed).
Why it matters: First credit-agency reaction to leadership turmoil; rating still very strong.

What happened: Anthropic IPOs at $83/share; Nvidia buys ~$10B of Class N shares in the concurrent $26B supplier placement alongside Google, AMD, Broadcom, Microsoft, Micron, TSMC.
Why it matters: Classic supplier-funds-customer pattern; public listing gives Nvidia a mark-to-market stake but also ties its portfolio to AI-lab valuations.

What happened: Reuters analysis: Nvidia turmoil marks end of easy money for AI trade; Nebius converts drop to 70 cents (>12% yield).
Why it matters: Funding stress at neoclouds that Nvidia owns stakes in and backstops.

What happened: Q1 FY27: revenue +30% to $19.3B, OCI +121%, RPO $664B, capex $28.5B, FCF -$5.4B; $20B ATM equity completed; FY27 capex guided $90-95B.
Why it matters: Shows the build is outrunning cash generation even with $11B of customer prepayments flattering operating cash flow.

What happened: Investor Day: FY30 revenue target $225B+, positive FCF in 2H FY28, $30B+ FCF FY29, $20B cap on new capital-markets funding; relies on vendor financing, BYO hardware, prepayments.
Why it matters: Moves part of the funding burden off Oracle's balance sheet onto suppliers and customers - exactly the hidden leverage a debt/EBITDA screen misses.

What happened: Oracle raises $20B ($10B stock at $116, $10B bonds at 7.0-8.65%); shares fall ~9%.
Why it matters: Entire 4-year funding cap used in one week at near-junk coupons; signals capital-market dependence and high cost of funds.

What happened: Project Jupiter (NM Stargate site for OpenAI) air-permit hearing vacated; Nov 23 decision deadline waived; no new date. Oracle had filed force majeure in Sept; HSBC dumped a construction-loan slice at a discount (Nov 16).
Why it matters: Power/permitting delays push revenue right while lease and financing costs keep accruing; lenders are already marking down exposure.

What happened: Bloomberg: Microsoft winding down 2023 deal to rent AI capacity from Oracle (older Nvidia GPUs). Oracle says older GPUs re-contracted at 20% premium.
Why it matters: Raises GPU obsolescence/re-leasing risk on hardware financed over 5+ years.

What happened: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns; CFO Colette Kress interim CEO, says Nvidia will be more selective on future investments/guarantees.
Why it matters: Nvidia is a key funder of OpenAI and likely vendor financier in Oracle's plan; any pullback weakens the circular financing loop.

What happened: Oracle CDS hits ~328bp; Oracle posts that its OpenAI contract is 'fully funded' including vendor financing and pre-emptively calls contrary reports 'wrong'.
Why it matters: Credit market prices Oracle near high-yield; 'fully funded' claim rests on undisclosed vendor financing.
